column1: # Claude's two passes (QUALITY.md end). Since 18 Nov every Hush Harbor story carries one 'say it with me' call and response at its turn (owner); each was read as part of the cultural pass: real church pairs (God is good / all the time, won't he do it / yes he will, our God is able / yes he is, glory / hallelujah) or 'Somebody say' plus a short line from the story, tied back to the story, never last.

column3: note
column5: note

column3: Same scripture and claims as the approved plain telling; the hymn line is Wesley (1740, public domain); no promised calm.
column5: Warm preaching cadence; the church mothers and the old saints are the community's memory, not an invented narrator's; ends on the story's truth; no dialect spellings.
column6: Cultural pass (coordinator review 18 Nov): the AI narrator had a first-person grandmother (invented person, R-PRF-02) and ended on 'Can I get an amen?'; now 'the church mothers' and the ending is the story's truth.

column3: Faithful to Exodus 14; the spirituals are named, not used as doctrine; credit stays with the LORD.
column5: The field songs are honoured as history, sung in hope; elders and children shown with dignity.

column3: Faithful to Daniel 6; 'keep on praying' encourages without promising the listener's rescue.
column5: The church mothers' saying rings true and is used once; the spiritual title is public domain.
column6: Cultural pass: 'a church mother I knew' was a first-person memory for an AI narrator; now 'the church mothers'.

column3: Faithful to Jonah 1-3; God's charge in the third person; 'God still knows your name' is assurance, not an outcome promise.
column5: One 'somebody ought to say amen'; plain grammar; sailors treated with respect.

column3: Faithful to 1 Samuel 17; says outright the story does not promise every battle ends this way.
column5: The saying is given to 'our grandmothers', the community, not an invented person.
column6: Cultural pass: dropped an invented framing name (Mother Johnson), then the first-person 'a church mother I knew'; now 'our grandmothers'.

column3: Faithful to Genesis 37 and 39:2; the brothers' sin is not softened.
column5: 'His daddy fussed' is plain speech, not dialect; Joseph's sale is told as the wrong it was.

column3: Faithful to Luke 15:11-32; no claim about the listener's standing; ends on the father going to both sons.
column5: Plain and warm; 'hogs' is everyday speech; the elder son is not mocked.

column3: Faithful to Ruth 1; Naomi's lament is allowed to stand.
column5: Two women's loyalty told with tenderness; the wedding line is accurate and kind.

column3: 'But if not' kept without promising rescue; no speculation on who the fourth man was.
column5: Steady, dignified young men; the elders' saying used once.

column3: Faithful to Mark 5:22-34 and 5:42; her healing stays hers in the text, no healing promise to the listener.
column5: She is seen, named daughter, never pitied; 'Church' used sparingly.

column3: Faithful to Genesis 6-9; 'God remembered Noah' is the text's own line; the rainbow spiritual is public domain and only its first line is used.
column5: Warm; 'do not despise a small leaf' fits the voice.
column6: Pastor pass: cut a speculation ('folks may have looked at him sideways') that the text does not give.

column3: Faithful to Esther 2-5; the fast is shown as the community standing with her, not a technique.
column5: Esther honoured as brave and wise; one call-out, mid-story.

column3: Faithful to Job 1-2 and 42; no reason for suffering invented; the old saying is given as what the elders said in trouble, not a promise.
column5: 'The repast' and the ministry of sitting are true to Black church grief; plain grammar outside the quoted saying.

column3: Faithful to Genesis 1:1-2:3; no side taken on how the days are read.
column5: 'You carry it' says the image of God plainly and with dignity, no race claim.

column3: Faithful to John 4; Jesus's identity stated as the text states it; her past not moralised.
column5: She becomes the town's witness; the one call-out sits before the close, not at the end.

column3: Faithful to Matthew 14:22-33; closes on what the disciples saw, not a promise.
column5: 'You do not need fancy words when you are going under' is warm and true.

column3: Faithful to Exodus 3:1-14; God's words only in KJV blocks.
column5: The spiritual is named, public domain; reverent.

column3: Faithful to Genesis 41-50 as cited; forgiveness does not excuse the sin.
column5: Tender, plain; the slave years named honestly.

column3: Faithful to Luke 10:38-42; no doctrine of women's roles added.
column5: 'Every church kitchen has a Martha, and thank God for her' honours service.

column3: Faithful to 1 Kings 17:1-16; states plainly it is not a formula; no seed-faith reading.
column5: The grandmothers who stretched a pot are honoured as a community, not pitied or mocked.

column3: Faithful to Genesis 2:7-3:23; calling the serpent's voice 'the enemy' is the common church reading, kept to one line, no doctrine of the fall built on it.
column5: Neither the man nor the woman is the villain; the call 'he came looking' sits at God's question.

column3: Faithful to 1 Samuel 1; says plainly the story does not promise every praying woman a child, and that waiting women are no less faithful.
column5: Childless women in the church honoured, not pitied; 'bless him' is warm, not mocking.

column3: Faithful to Luke 19:1-10; grace before change; no prosperity reading.
column5: 'Make haste' call is the verse's own word; his height told without mockery.

column3: Faithful to Mark 2:1-12; no promise of healing to the listener.
column5: Disability shown with dignity; 'carry somebody' honours the friends, not pity.

column3: Faithful to Luke 2:1-20; no extra-biblical characters.
column5: The spiritual is named (public domain); working people honoured.

column3: Faithful to Judges 4:1-16 and 5:1-3; Jael's act not retold; Barak's request given two readings.
column5: A woman judge with full authority; 'won't he do it' tied to the LORD going out before them, in the story's past.

column3: Faithful to 2 Kings 4:1-7; says plainly it is not a promise that giving makes anyone rich; no seed-faith reading.
column5: The widow is resourceful, the neighbours honoured.

column3: Faithful to Genesis 12 and 15; 'he believed' is the text's own point; no quick-answer promise.
column5: An old man starting over, told with dignity.

column3: Faithful to Luke 10:25-37; 'church folks' for the priest and Levite is the parable's own sting, not added contempt.
column5: Jews and Samaritans both described with respect.

column3: Faithful to Exodus 1-2 as cited.
column5: Three women honoured; 'look at God' tied to the mother getting her baby back.

column3: Faithful to 1 Sam 18:1-4 and 20:35-42; the spear is 20:33, the kindness to Jonathan's son 2 Sam 9; covenant friendship only, nothing read into it.
column5: Warm preaching cadence; men's tears honoured without a joke; 'his own daddy' once, natural; call and response 'he held nothing back' tied to the gifts, not last.

column3: Faithful to John 11:17-44 (v3 and v6 in narration); Jesus's words only as scripture; no promise that a listener's dead will be raised now; the 'fourth day' folk belief left out as unprovable.
column5: A house in grief drawn the way Black families keep it (food, quiet, sitting with the family) without stereotype; 'I believe' at Martha's confession.

column3: Faithful to Judges 6:11-16 and 7:2-8 (6:2-5 and the 32,000 of 7:3 in narration); God's words read as scripture; the close is 'he will be with you', the text's promise to Gideon, not an outcome.
column5: Honest questions to God honoured; 'mighty man of valour' as the call; no caricature.

column3: Faithful to Mark 5:21-24 and 35-43 (the woman of 25-34 named in passing; Peter, James, John from v37); no promise that a sick child will be healed.
column5: A father's love shown with dignity; 'only believe' at the turn; the food at the end kept tender.

column3: Faithful to Gen 32:6-12 and 33:1-11 (32:7-8 split camps, 33:3 seven bows); reconciliation urged gently, with prayer first, never as a guarantee.
column5: Family estrangement spoken to plainly and kindly; 'Esau ran' as the response.

column3: Faithful to John 6:1-14; the boy and barley from v9; 'two hundred pennyworth' explained as most of a year's wages; no promise of provision beyond the story's own.
column5: 'Our God is able / yes he is', a real church pair; the boy's small gift honoured; no poverty-only framing.

column3: Faithful to 1 Sam 3:1-10; Hannah from 1 Sam 1; God's call read as scripture; Eli's instruction voiced by Eli; v1 put in narration in our own words (no typed verse).
column5: The old saints teaching the young to hear God, without any invented person; 'speak, Lord' at the turn.

column3: Faithful to 1 Kings 3:16-28 (3:9 for the request); James 1:5 in our own words without a reference; the women's trade left in the stored verse.
column5: Both mothers shown as people; a mother's love honoured; the king credited to God.

column3: Faithful to Mark 10:46-52; 'be of good comfort, rise' is v49 in the stored verse; no promise of healing to the listener.
column5: A blind beggar with agency; 'he cried the more' at the turn; the cloak line warm and real.

column3: Faithful to Exod 19:16-20 and 20:1-17; the commandments only as scripture blocks; rest named without a position on which day; deliverance before law, as 20:2.
column5: The freedom story the Black church preaches, told without claiming any people's history as its own; 'he brought us out' at the turn.

column3: Faithful to Matt 25:14-29; stops before v30; says outright nobody in the parable got a promise of money (no prosperity reading); 'well done' as the master's word, not a promise to the listener of reward.
column5: Preaching cadence without caricature; 'well done' at the turn; the fearful servant not mocked.

column3: Faithful to Josh 2:1-21; Rahab in Christ's line is Matt 1:5 and her faith Heb 11:31, in words; her trade left in the stored verse; v11 confessed in our own words (no typed verse).
column5: Rahab honoured as a woman of faith who stood in the gap for her family; never a joke about her past.

column3: Faithful to Josh 6:1-20; God's commands as scripture; the spiritual 'Joshua Fit the Battle of Jericho' (traditional, public domain) named with one line; ends at v20, no gloating over the city; no promise the listener's walls will fall.
column5: 'I have given' at the turn; walking in obedience preached warmly and plainly.

column3: Faithful to John 3:1-17; water and Spirit not interpreted (no baptism position); John 7:50 and 19:39 for the later Nicodemus; no telling the listener she is saved or lost.
column5: A seeker honoured; 'bring your questions' is the church's welcome, not a pitch.

column3: Faithful to 1 Sam 25:14-35 (v22 and v34 left out by verse choice); credit to God as David gives it.
column5: 'She made haste' at the turn; Abigail's wisdom and courage honoured; 'pray while they pack' warm, not a stereotype.

column3: Faithful to 1 Kings 19:1-15 (450 prophets 18:22, 7,000 v18); Elijah's wish to die told gently; ends pointing a weary listener to someone who loves her; no outcome promised.
column5: 'Arise and eat' at the turn; 'y'all' once, natural speech; despair never shamed.

column3: Faithful to Mark 10:17-27; 'young' and 'ruler' attributed to Matthew and Luke; no rule that all must sell everything; v27 told in our own words.
column5: 'He came running' at the turn; the rich man sincere and sad, not mocked.

column3: Faithful to Gen 24:10-27; v16 skipped; the servant's prayer and thanks kept as scripture, v27 echoed in our own words.
column5: 'Before he had done speaking' at the turn; Rebekah's kindness and labour honoured, no romance gloss.

column3: Faithful to Judges 16:4-30; tagged violence strong, adult; his vengeance (v28) not praised; Heb 11:32 in words; v20 told in our own words.
column5: 'Watch your heart' at the turn; Delilah shown as bought, not a seductress caricature; no sexual detail.

column3: Faithful to Matt 2:1-12; stops before v16; the wise men's number and rank not invented.
column5: 'Come to worship' at the turn; strangers from the east honoured.

column3: Faithful to John 2:1-11; nothing for or against drinking; Mary's word kept as scripture; 'woman' explained as respectful.
column5: 'Do it' at the turn, Mary's word; the servants honoured as the ones who saw; family celebration drawn warmly.

column3: Faithful to Num 22:21-35; the angel of the LORD read only by the narrator; set-up and blessings (22:1-20, 23-24) told without invented speech.
column5: 'God is in the way' at the turn; humour aimed at pride, never at any people.

column3: Faithful to Luke 15:1-7; the grumblers' complaint turned to praise without scorn for them; no claim on who is lost tonight.
column5: 'He went after the one' at the turn; tax collectors and sinners welcomed.

column3: Faithful to Gen 29:9-30, tagged sexual implied (v23 left out); Leah seen by God is v31 and her sons' names vv32-35; Judah to David to Jesus stated without references; 'reaped what he had sown' is Gal 6:7's sense, not a promise.
column5: Leah honoured, never a joke about looks; 'love makes the years short' tied to v20.

column3: Faithful to Luke 16:19-31; says it is not a map of the life to come; no one told she is bound anywhere; the sin named is neglect.
column5: 'God sees' at the turn; the poor man has the name and the dignity.

column3: Faithful to John 13:1-17; no position on foot washing as an ordinance.
column5: 'He took a towel' at the turn; service as love, not servitude.

column3: Faithful to Acts 9:1-19; the Lord's words read by the narrator; v18 baptism left in the verse without comment.
column5: 'He knows my name' at the turn; Ananias the ordinary believer honoured.

column3: Faithful to Luke 23:33-47, violence mild and off the page; no blame of 'the Jews'; 'Were You There' is a traditional spiritual (public domain), named with its own line.
column5: 'Father, forgive them' at the turn; reverent Good Friday cadence; 'Sunday is coming' as the church says it.

column3: Faithful to John 20:1-18; the Sabbath named only as the day between; the other disciple left unnamed.
column5: 'He called my name' at the turn, after v16; Mary Magdalene honoured as first witness, no legends.

column3: Faithful to Luke 24:13-35; breaking of bread told as the text tells it, no position on communion.
column5: 'Abide with us' at the turn, the disciples' own plea; grief honoured.

column3: Faithful to Gen 16:1-13 and 21:14-19 (16:12 left out); tagged sexual implied (16:4 in the verse, not dwelt on); 16:9's hard word kept and named as hard, never used to bless servitude; the angel's words read by the narrator.
column5: Hagar honoured as an African woman God called by name, with agency and grief; no servant-only framing; 'he sees me' tied to 16:13; the close speaks to used and sent-away women without pity.

column3: Faithful to Acts 8:26-39; v37 kept as the KJV has it, no comment; baptism (v36, v38) left in the verses with no position; 'Africa' is geography (Ethiopia/Cush), not a claim about anyone's colour.
column5: An African official shown with learning, authority and humility; 'God is good / all the time'; no exoticising.

column3: Faithful to Exod 5:1-2, 7:14-16, 12:31-32; God's word through Moses read by the narrator; the plagues and Passover told in order from Exod 5:6-12:30 without invented speech.
column5: The freedom story told as enslaved Black Americans sang it ('Go Down, Moses', traditional), in the third person, never a narrator claiming 'our people'; Pharaoh not caricatured.

column3: Faithful to Jer 38:6-13; the set-up (38:1-5) and God's word to him (39:15-18) told in words; nothing invented about him beyond the text.
column5: An Ethiopian with courage and gentleness; 'servant of the king' meaning given with dignity, no servitude framing; 'somebody heard' at the turn.

column3: Faithful to Mark 15:20-22 and Luke 23:26-27; crucifixion morning tagged violence mild, no wound detail; Rufus of Rom 16:13 offered only as 'nobody can say for sure'; 'Must Jesus Bear the Cross Alone' is a public-domain hymn.
column5: Simon shown from North Africa without any claim about his colour; compelled, not servile; 'he carried it' at the turn.

column3: Faithful to 1 Kings 10:1-10; Sheba's place given both ways (Ethiopian tradition and Arabia), no ethnicity stated as history; Matt 12:42 in words.
column5: A queen of power and learning, honoured; no exoticising or romance gloss; 'she came to see' at the turn.

column3: Faithful to Num 12:1-15; God's words read by the narrator; says only what the text says (God rebukes the speakers and says nothing against the wife); no reading of the leprosy as a racial sign.
column5: The Cushite wife defended with dignity; Miriam not demonised, the camp waits for her; 'the LORD heard it' at the turn.

column3: Faithful to Exod 2:15-22; 2:11-12 told in our own words; whether Zipporah is the Cushite of Num 12 left open, as the text leaves it; Exod 4:24-26 named only as her quick act.
column5: Hospitality and the stranger honoured; Zipporah given her place; 'he stood up' at the turn.

column3: Faithful to Acts 16:22-34; the jailer's despair told gently and Paul's 'do thyself no harm' kept as care; baptism left in the verse; no promise that the listener's chains will fall.
column5: The old saints' singing in chains named in the third person; 'at midnight' at the turn; warm and real.

column3: Faithful to Ezek 37:1-14 (Ezekiel's first person stays in the stored verses, read by the narrator); applied to lost hope with 'Lord, you know', no promise of an outcome.
column5: 'Very dry' at the turn; 'Dem Bones' (1928, public domain) echoed in plain spelling, no dialect; hopeful, not preachy.

column3: Faithful to John 5:1-9; v4 kept as the KJV has it, no comment; Jesus's words only as scripture; 'impotent' left in the verse, 'sick' in narration; no promise of healing to the listener.
column5: 'Wade in the Water' (traditional) named as the old saints' song, in the third person; no contested escape-code claim; the lonely man honoured.

column3: Faithful to Gen 32:24-30; the wrestler's words read by the narrator (God is never voiced); the name meaning from Gen 25:26 and 27:36.
column5: 'Till daybreak' at the turn; holding on to God preached plainly, the limp honoured.

column3: Faithful to 2 Kings 2:1-14 (the sons of the prophets of vv3, 5 told in words); double portion explained from Deut 21:17's sense; no promise about any listener's loved ones.
column5: 'Swing Low, Sweet Chariot' (traditional) named as the old saints' song; grief for the elders honoured; 'I will not leave thee' at the turn.

column3: Faithful to 2 Kings 4:8-37 (vv13-15, 19, 24, 29, 31 told in words or left out); the close says plainly that God does not promise every story ends this way.
column5: A great woman shown with means, faith and grief; 'It Is Well with My Soul' (1873, public domain) named; 'it is well' at the turn.

column3: Faithful to 2 Kings 5:1-14 (vv5-8 told in words); Elisha's word through a messenger read by the narrator; no healing promise.
column5: The captive girl and the servants honoured as the wise ones; 'but' at the turn, a real preaching device.

column3: Faithful to Luke 13:10-17; the Sabbath dispute told as the text tells it with no position on which day; 'whom Satan hath bound' left in the verse without a doctrine of illness; points women carrying abuse to a pastor, counselor, doctor or friend.
column5: 'Woman, thou art loosed' named as a sentence Black churches preach, no person named; women's burdens listed with care, never pity.

column3: Faithful to 2 Sam 9:1-13; the covenant is 1 Sam 20:14-17, the fall 2 Sam 4:4; grace preached without a claim on anyone's salvation.
column5: Disability honoured (his feet are part of him at the table, not fixed); 'for Jonathan's sake' at the turn; no shame.

column3: Faithful to 2 Chr 20:1-22 (vv23-25 told in words); Jahaziel's prophecy read by the narrator; 'prosper' (v20) left in the verse and the close says God never promised we would not face battles; 'The Battle Is Not Yours' named only as what choirs sing.
column5: Praise before the victory, preached plainly; 'God is good / all the time'.

column3: Faithful to Neh 2:11-20 and 6:15-16 (Nehemiah's first person stays in the verses); 1:4, 4:17 and 6:3 told in our own words; no prosperity reading of 2:20.
column5: 'Rise up and build' at the turn; communities rebuilding honoured without stereotype.

column3: Faithful to Acts 12:5-17; the angel read by the narrator; James's death (12:2) told in our own words; no promise that every prayer is answered this way.
column5: Rhoda, the young servant nobody believed, honoured; the prayer meeting tradition warm and real; 'prayer was made' at the turn.
